title: Rate limiting for the Orders API, line by line
subtitle: feature/rate-limit → main · simple style

scenes.narration: This change does three things. It limits how many orders one address can send per minute. It prices each item from the pricing service. And it sends an event for every new order. There are no tests.
scenes.summary: Limit POST /orders to 20 per minute per IP, price items from the pricing service, and publish order.created.
bullets: If Redis is down, every order request fails
The event is sent after the save, so a queue error fails a saved order
No tests cover the limiter, the prices, or the event

scenes.narration: Here is the system. A client calls the Express A P I. It asks Redis to count the request. The orders service prices and saves the order. Then the A P I tells the queue.

steps.say: First the A P I counts it in Redis.
Then create order prices and saves the order.
Last, the A P I publishes the event and does not wait. Then it answers the client.

scenes.title: POST /orders
scenes.narration: Here is the data at each step.

steps.say: The limiter counts the request.
The service prices every item.
Then it saves the order.
The A P I publishes a small event.
Then it answers the client.

scenes.narration: Before the change, look at the database client. The orders service uses it to save orders. This file does not change.

steps.say: Line one defines the d b object. It is the database client.
Insert takes a table name and a row. It returns the row with a new id.

scenes.narration: This is the new rate limit file. It has one function. Let us read it from the top.

steps.say: Line one imports the request types from Express. Line two imports the Redis client. Redis is a fast store for small values.
Lines four and five start the options type. Window m s is the length of one time window, in milliseconds.
Line six is max. It is the number of requests allowed in one window. Line seven closes the type.
Line nine defines the rate limit function. It takes the options. Line ten returns a middleware. A middleware is a function that runs before the route.

scenes.narration: Now the body of the middleware. It runs once for every request to the orders route. First it counts the request.
scenes.calloutText: The key expires with the window, so Redis cleans it up.

steps.say: Line eleven builds a key. The key has the I P address and the current minute. So each address gets a new key every minute.
steps.label: Build a key for this address and minute

steps.say: Line twelve adds one to the count for that key in Redis. Redis returns the new count.
steps.label: Count the request in Redis

steps.say: Line thirteen runs only on the first request in a window. It tells Redis to delete the key after one minute.
steps.label: On the first hit, expire the key after a minute

scenes.narration: The count decides what happens next.
scenes.calloutText: Retry-After tells the client how many seconds to wait.

steps.say: Line fourteen checks the count. Max is twenty. So this is true from the twenty first request on.
steps.label: Is the count over the limit?

steps.say: Line fifteen adds a Retry After header. It tells the client to wait sixty seconds. Line sixteen answers with status four twenty nine. That means too many requests.
steps.label: Refuse with Retry-After and 429

steps.say: Line seventeen closes the if. Line eighteen calls next. That lets the request go on to the route.
steps.label: Under the limit, pass the request on

steps.say: Lines nineteen and twenty close the middleware and the function.
steps.label: End of the function

scenes.narration: This is the server file. Four lines are new.
scenes.calloutText: publish runs after the insert, so a queue error fails a saved order.

steps.say: Line three imports the rate limit function.
Line four imports publish from the queue module.
Line eight puts the limiter on the orders path. The window is sixty thousand milliseconds. That is one minute. Max is twenty.
Line twelve runs after the order is saved. It publishes an order created event with the order id and the total.

scenes.narration: This is the orders service. It used a fixed price of ten. Now it asks the pricing service.
scenes.calloutText: Pricing lookups run in parallel with Promise.all.

steps.say: Line two imports price for from the pricing module.
The old lines nine and ten are removed. They priced every item at ten and saved the order.
The new line ten rejects an empty order. It throws an error.
Line eleven asks the price of each item. The calls run at the same time with Promise all.
Line twelve adds up quantity times price for each item. That is the total.
Line thirteen saves the order with the total and a status of pending.

scenes.narration: This is the new queue module.

steps.say: The publish function takes a topic and a payload. Today it only logs them. A real queue would come later.

scenes.narration: This old file is deleted. Nothing imported it any more.

steps.say: The old throttle kept a map of counts in memory. It counted hits per key.
It allowed up to one hundred hits per key. Memory is lost on restart, so Redis replaces it.

scenes.title: Test coverage
scenes.subject: rateLimit, createOrder and the orders route
scenes.narration: This change adds no tests. Nothing checks the limit, the prices, or the event. The gaps are listed here.
gaps: The twenty first request in a minute from one IP gets 429 with a Retry-After header
When Redis is down the limiter throws, so every order request fails
When the queue is down after the insert, the client gets an error for a saved order
Empty orders are rejected and totals use prices from the pricing service
